THIS WRIT PETITION (CIVIL) HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 09.07.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 3 WP(C) NO.18101 OF 2019 2025:KER:53873  JUDGMENT Petitioner points out an unfortunate instance, in which his wife was electrocuted on 08.05.2018, as seen from Ext.P3 investigation report, while she was removing the input plug of an inverter (UPS)
allegedly manufactured by the 4th respondent company.
The following prayers have been raised in the writ petition.

"I. Issue a writ of mandamus, or any other appropriate writ or direction to the 6th Respondent to include Inverter/Uninterruptible Power Systems (UPS) in the Schedule of the Household Electrical Appliances (Quality Control) Order, 1981.
Zainudheen.S.A vs State Of Kerala on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191274461/
2 II. Issue a writ of mandamus, or any other appropriate writ or direction to the 6th Respondent and the 1st Respondent, to empower the 2nd Respondent, to monitor the manufacture, storage, sale and distribution of Inverters/Uninterruptible Power Systems (UPS) in the State until necessary Orders are made to include Inverters in the Household Electrical Appliances (Quality Control) Order, 1981.

III. Issue any appropriate writ or direction to the 4 th Respondent, to issue compensation of Twenty-Five Lakh Rupees to the petitioner.
WP(C) NO.18101 OF 2019 2025:KER:53873 IV. Issue any appropriate writ or direction to the 5 th Respondent, to issue compensation of Five Lakh Rupees to the petitioner."
2.

I have heard Sri.Rahul Sudheesh, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri.K.R.Vinod, learned counsel for the 4th respondent, Sri.T.K.Sandeep, learned counsel for the 5th respondent,
Sri.E.G.Gorden, learned Senior Government Pleader for the 1st respondent and Sri.C.Dinesh, the learned Central Government Counsel for the 6th respondent.

3. As regards the prayer for compensation on the basis of the allegation noticed as above, I am of the opinion that the award of compensation can be had only after proper adducing of evidence and appreciation thereon.
This is not possible in a writ jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
4. Sri.Rahul, learned counsel for the petitioner, in such circumstances, seeks liberty to raise a question as regards the compensation before the appropriate forum.

5. As regards the larger prayers, this Court notices that, ultimately, it is for the 6th respondent to consider the afore WP(C) NO.18101 OF 2019 2025:KER:53873 whether to include the invertor/UPS in the schedule of the Household Electrical Appliances (Quality Control Order, 1981).

I permit the petitioner to make an appropriate representation before the 6th respondent herein pointing out the requirement for carrying out such an inclusion, within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

If such a representation is made, needless to say, the 6th respondent would take into account the circumstances pointed out by the petitioner and do the needful in the matter within a further period of six months thereafter.

As regards the prayer for compensation, noticing the submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioner, liberty is granted to the petitioner to approach the competent authority seeking compensation, if so advised,
in accordance with law.

Sd/-
